description: We are three students from TED Kdz. Eregli College, Türkiye, with a shared interest in space and storytelling. Through “Abandoned but Not Forgotten,” we aim to bring the stories of NASA’s space equipment to life and help young people discover the science and legacy behind it. We are excited to learn, create, and explore together!
summary: Hayabusa: A Small Capsule, a Lasting Legacy is an educational digital story for school-age learners. Narrated from the spacecraft’s perspective, it follows Japan’s Hayabusa mission to asteroid Itokawa, its technical challenges, and its return of asteroid samples to Earth. Drawing on NASA and JAXA resources, the story connects scientific facts with imaginative storytelling to explore perseverance, discovery, and the legacy of space exploration.
details:
Our project tells the story of Hayabusa, Japan’s asteroid explorer, through an imagined first-person narrative supported by factual mission information.

Designed for school-age learners, the story follows Hayabusa’s journey to asteroid Itokawa, the technical difficulties it faced, and the return of its sample capsule to Earth in 2010. We use storytelling to explain why asteroid samples matter and how engineers used teamwork and creative problem-solving to overcome challenges.

Our project combines a written narrative with a seven-slide presentation introducing the mission and sharing an excerpt from the story. The spacecraft’s thoughts and emotions are fictional; the mission events and scientific information are based on NASA and JAXA resources.

Hayabusa returned the first samples collected from an asteroid. Its main spacecraft burned up during atmospheric re-entry, while the sample capsule reached Earth. Our central message is that a mission can end while its scientific legacy continues.

Hayabusa was a Japanese mission, with support from NASA. We distinguish the mission’s actual history from the imaginative voice used in our story.
